title: Let's Talk About FOMAT: Fear of Missing Agent Time — Michael Richman, Cmd+Ctrl
talk_summary: Michael Richman presents 'Command and Control,' a daemon + control-plane + mobile/web UI system that aggregates coding-agent sessions across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, etc., so a human can monitor state, get push notifications when an agent is blocked or done, and start/resume sessions from anywhere. The core insight is that agents are not actually autonomous—they stall waiting for input—and the human's attention, not agent time, is the scarce resource.

takeaways.what_they_do: A per-agent daemon watches the agent lifecycle and reports state changes (blocked/needs-help/done) to a control plane, which pushes notifications to the human instead of requiring polling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They monitor life cycle of the agent. When things change, it's blocked, it needs your help. It communicates up to the control plane layer

takeaways.technique: Single pane of glass across heterogeneous agents
takeaways.what_they_do: One control plane aggregates sessions regardless of framework or machine (local Mac vs cloud VM) into one UI, so the operator doesn't context-switch between terminals.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I needed a system that is a single pane of glass into all of my agent sessions. Regardless of which platform they're running on, regardless of what machine they are on.

takeaways.what_they_do: Sessions are grouped into 'subscribe for push', 'on my radar', 'recent 24h', and the rest, so thousands of sessions are triaged by attention level rather than flat-listed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This is all of my sessions grouped by ones I want notifications for and ones that I want to keep my eye on and recent ones.

takeaways.technique: LLM stand-up summary of recent sessions
takeaways.what_they_do: An overview dashboard summarizes the last several messages of each recent session into a stand-up-style digest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can get a kind of stand-up summary of the most recent sessions. And this is just using the last several messages

takeaways.what_they_do: The UI can launch a new agent session or resume an existing one from phone/web, picking any configured agent and working directory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can start a new session right from the command and control UI. I can pick any configured agent

takeaways.technique: Attention as the bottleneck, not agent time
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames the real constraint as human cognitive load and unpredictable need-for-input, arguing for systems that reach the human wherever they are rather than maximizing raw agent parallelism.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The cognitive load of managing multiple agent sessions is really high. And it is exhausting
